hints: Focus on what type of reducing agent $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is and how far it reduces a carboxylic acid.
Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, is reduced all the way to its primary alcohol, propan-1-ol.
Think of the second step as esterification where methanoic acid provides the $\text{HCOO}$ part and P provides the alcohol part.
walkthrough:
**Reduce propanoic acid to P**

Think of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ as a very strong reducing agent. It reduces carboxylic acids completely to primary alcohols, not stopping at the aldehyde.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
So product P is propan-1-ol.

**Esterify P with methanoic acid to make Q**

A carboxylic acid plus an alcohol with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives an ester plus water. Here the acid is methanoic acid and the alcohol is P.

$$\text{HCOOH} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So product Q is propyl methanoate.

**Match to skeletal formulae**

P must show a 3-carbon chain ending in $\text{OH}$, and Q must show $\text{H-C(=O)-O-}$ joined to a 3-carbon propyl group. Only one row shows both of these correctly.

options.A: P is correct as propan-1-ol, but Q is wrong. This Q is methyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. It swaps the roles, using propanoic acid as the acid part and methanol as the alcohol part. In our reaction the acid part must come from methanoic acid.
options.B: Both are correct. P is propan-1-ol from complete reduction of propanoic acid by $\text{LiAlH}_4$. Q is propyl methanoate, $\text{HCOOPr}$, from esterification of methanoic acid with propan-1-ol. The skeletal formulae match perfectly.
options.C: Both are wrong. P is shown as propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. This is the trap of stopping reduction at the aldehyde, but $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces acids fully to primary alcohols. Q is methyl propanoate, which also swaps the acid and alcohol fragments.
options.D: Q is correct as propyl methanoate, but P is wrong. P is shown as propanal. Remember, aldehydes are made by partial reduction of acid chlorides or oxidation of primary alcohols, not by $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduction of carboxylic acids which goes all the way to the alcohol.
